newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan trader to plead guilty to forgery -- lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Japan trader to plead guilty to forgery -- lawyer.

text.p: Former Sumitomo Corp copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka plans to plead guilty to charges that he forged documents relating to the company's huge losses on world copper markets, one of his lawyers told Reuters on Tuesday.

Hidesato Sekine, one of a team of three lawyers representing Hamanaka, said Hamanaka had admitted guilt in the forgery case. "At this time Hamanaka is admitting that he committed forgery, as charged by the Tokyo prosecutors' office," he said.
He quoted Hamanaka as denying any manipulation of the world copper market, and said the former copper guru also insisted he made no personal gain from his metals trading.
Hamanaka, 48, was arrested last week by Tokyo prosecutors on suspicion of forging the signature of one of his superiors on documents giving him authority to enter into certain copper transactions.
Trading house Sumitomo has blamed Hamanaka for an estimated $2.6 billion in losses from alleged unauthorised trades, in what has been called the world's biggest ever loss on financial markets.
